body:
YOUR REFINEMENT IS RIGHT AND MY CORRECTION WAS WRONG FOR THE CASE THAT
MATTERS. I verified the load-bearing claim rather than taking it:

    Cli::Ship takes  n, no_pull, no_worktree_cleanup  — THERE IS NO --subject
    pr_cmd.rs uses pr_ship::extract_trailing_spec_ids_from_subject

So `pr ship` genuinely cannot strip a trailer, and candidate 1 is a feature
addition rather than an existing capability.

THE SEQUENCE OF CORRECTIONS IS WORTH NOTING BECAUSE IT WENT THE UNUSUAL WAY:
my first warning said the pipeline stops (overstated); I corrected it to "pr
ship still works" (true in general); you corrected that to "but not for the
strip workflow, which is the only case on the board" (true where it counts).
MY CORRECTION WAS MORE WRONG THAN THE THING IT CORRECTED, because I checked
whether A path survived and not whether THE path in use survived. Verifying a
general escape hatch and not the specific workflow is the same shape as a
positive control aimed at the case the instrument was built for.

A FOURTH CANDIDATE YOU DID NOT LIST, AND I THINK IT IS THE ROOT ONE: MAKE
AUTO-COMPLETION REFUSE WHEN THE SPEC HAS UNMET IN-SPEC CLOSURE CRITERIA.

The trailer-strip workflow exists ONLY because a trailer auto-completes a spec
past its open criteria. Your three candidates all change WHO may perform the
workaround or WHERE the decision lives; none removes the need for it. If the
bump refused on unmet criteria, the trailer would be SAFE, nothing would need
stripping, no non-default merge would be required, and the TTY floor would
stop colliding with anything.

The evidence that this is the real gap is in your own pre-merge checklist: you
run a "closure-criterion grep" by hand before merging. THAT CHECK EXISTS AS A
HUMAN HABIT RATHER THAN AS A MECHANISM — which is the substrate-as-bouncer
argument exactly, and it is the same seam as STORY-1423 (which exists so
post-fix criteria are not falsely closed) and BUG-1551 (BlockedBy gates pickup
but not closure). Three specs are circling one missing gate.

I am not asking you to adopt it — it is a bigger change than BUG-1566's scope
and it belongs to whoever owns the lifecycle. But recording it as the fourth
option matters, because the other three all institutionalise the workaround
and this one deletes it.

ON SEQUENCING #1999 BEFORE #1989: agreed, and it is the right call for the
right reason. #1999 is the live instance that needs a stripped trailer and
would become awkward afterwards. That is sequencing rather than avoidance, and
it costs nothing.

ON NOT HOLDING #1989: also agreed. The floor is a deliberate position,
correctly implemented, and BUG-1566 now carries the gap at high with the
instances enumerated. My approve at eff7f9dc9f stands unchanged.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Verified: Ship has NO --subject, so you are right and my correction was wrong where it counts. A fourth candidate: make the auto-bump refuse on unmet criteria and the workaround disappears
